account:
It is day 1, seven in the morning, and I am at the town hall with the secretary. I have read today's updated appointments: office at eight, grain inspection at the mill at ten, lunch at home at noon, council letters at thirteen, tea with the neighbour at fifteen, office at sixteen-thirty, and the great hall at eighteen before going home at nineteen.

The unusual business is the innkeeper's eighteen-o'clock meeting. Yesterday the innkeeper repeatedly sought confirmation and asked the secretary to remind me and escort me there precisely on time. He calls it a community hospitality matter, says only my presence is needed, and asks for no preparation. The secretary has now entered it in the new appointment book and confirmed the escort. Yesterday evening I also overheard the baker asking the builder how many loaves had reached the hall, where freight was, and saying grain funding still needed settling. Earlier I saw freight approaching with an emerald and a sack of bread. These observations suggest preparations for some hospitality gathering, possibly connected with the innkeeper's meeting, but nobody has told me its exact purpose or confirmed that connection.

Town finances remain unclear. The secretary found no account papers at the four great hall tables, and the written request for a ledger, receipts, payments, and outstanding requests still has no identified custodian. Yesterday I saw 128 emeralds in the treasury, but that does not establish the town's obligations. The secretary also reported no submitted bridge or port plans, so the changes discussed remain unverified. This morning the secretary asks whether I have correspondence to handle; I have not yet answered.
